ema.title: EMA {period} Distance Guide
ema.whatItIs: EMA (Exponential Moving Average) {period} is a trend-following indicator that gives more weight to recent prices. It smooths out price action and helps identify the overall trend direction. When price is above EMA, it suggests bullish momentum; below suggests bearish momentum. The distance from EMA indicates how extended the price is from its average.
ema.aboveEma: Price is {distance} points ABOVE EMA ({pct}% above). This indicates bullish momentum - buyers are in control.
ema.belowEma: Price is {distance} points BELOW EMA ({pct}% below). This indicates bearish momentum - sellers are in control.
ema.touchReactionBullish: In an uptrend, EMA often acts as dynamic SUPPORT. Expect a bounce upward. This is a potential BUY zone.
ema.touchReactionBearish: In a downtrend, EMA often acts as dynamic RESISTANCE. Expect rejection downward. This is a potential SELL zone.
ema.breakReactionBullish: Breaking above EMA signals potential trend reversal to bullish. Wait for confirmation before entering.
ema.breakReactionBearish: Breaking below EMA signals potential trend reversal to bearish. Consider reducing long positions.
ema.tip20: EMA 20 is best for short-term trends and scalping. It reacts quickly to price changes.
ema.tip50: EMA 50 is the medium-term trend indicator. Institutional traders watch this level closely.
ema.tip200: EMA 200 is the long-term trend indicator. A price above EMA 200 = bull market, below = bear market.
ema.tipClose: Price is very close to EMA - expect a reaction soon. Watch for bounce or break.
ema.tipFar: Price is extended far from EMA - mean reversion likely. Consider taking profits.
ema.tipMid: Price is at moderate distance from EMA - trend is healthy, no immediate action needed.
ema.tipGeneral: Always confirm EMA signals with volume and other indicators before trading.

channel.title: Trend Channel Guide
channel.whatItIs: A trend channel consists of two parallel lines containing price action - an upper resistance line and a lower support line. Price tends to bounce between these boundaries. Channel width indicates volatility, slope shows trend direction, and R² measures how well price respects the channel.
channel.uptrendStatus: UPTREND channel active with {strength}% strength. Price is moving in a controlled bullish pattern.
channel.downtrendStatus: DOWNTREND channel active with {strength}% strength. Price is moving in a controlled bearish pattern.
channel.upperCondition: If price reaches upper channel boundary
channel.upperReaction: Upper band = RESISTANCE zone. Expect a pullback or consolidation. Consider taking partial profits on longs or look for short entries.
channel.lowerCondition: If price reaches lower channel boundary
channel.lowerReaction: Lower band = SUPPORT zone. Expect a bounce upward. This is an optimal BUY zone within the channel.
channel.breakoutCondition: If price breaks out of channel
channel.breakoutReactionUp: Breakout above upper band = Trend acceleration. New highs likely. Consider adding to long positions.
channel.breakoutReactionDown: Breakdown below lower band = Trend reversal warning. New lows likely. Exit longs, consider shorts.
channel.tipUpperHalf: Price is in the upper half of channel - closer to resistance. Be cautious with new long entries.
channel.tipLowerHalf: Price is in the lower half of channel - closer to support. Better zone for long entries.
channel.tipStrong: Channel has strong R² correlation - boundaries are more reliable for trading decisions.
channel.tipWeak: Channel has weak correlation - boundaries may not hold. Use tighter stops.
channel.tipGeneral: Best strategy: Buy at lower band, sell at upper band. Place stops outside channel boundaries.

sr.whatIsSupport: A SUPPORT level is a price zone where buying pressure historically overwhelms selling pressure, causing price to bounce upward. The more times price has bounced from this level (touches), the stronger and more reliable it becomes. Support acts as a 'floor' for price.
sr.whatIsResistance: A RESISTANCE level is a price zone where selling pressure historically overwhelms buying pressure, causing price to reverse downward. The more times price has rejected from this level (touches), the stronger and more reliable it becomes. Resistance acts as a 'ceiling' for price.
sr.touchSupportCondition: If price reaches this support level
sr.touchSupportReaction: Expect BUYING pressure and a bounce upward. This is a potential LONG entry zone. Place stop-loss below the support level.
sr.touchResistanceCondition: If price reaches this resistance level
sr.touchResistanceReaction: Expect SELLING pressure and a rejection downward. This is a potential SHORT entry zone or profit-taking area for longs.
sr.breakSupportCondition: If price breaks below this support
sr.breakSupportReaction: Support becomes RESISTANCE. Expect further downside. Old support level becomes new short entry zone on retest.
sr.breakResistanceCondition: If price breaks above this resistance
sr.breakResistanceReaction: Resistance becomes SUPPORT. Expect further upside. Old resistance level becomes new long entry zone on retest.
sr.tip1: This level has been tested {hits} times - each touch adds to its significance.
sr.tipClose: Price is very close to this level - expect a reaction within the next few candles.
sr.tipFar: Price is far from this level - no immediate action. Monitor as price approaches.
sr.tipStrong: This is a STRONG level - higher probability of holding. Good for larger position sizes.
sr.tipWeak: This is a WEAK level - may break easily. Use smaller position sizes and tighter stops.

doubleBottom.name: Double Bottom
doubleBottom.description: A bullish reversal pattern that forms after a downtrend. Price touches a support level twice, creating a 'W' shape.
doubleBottom.afterCompletion: After the neckline breaks, expect an upward move equal to the pattern height. Target = Neckline + (Neckline - Bottom).
doubleBottom.tradingTip: Wait for neckline break with volume confirmation. Place stop below the second bottom.

doubleTop.name: Double Top
doubleTop.description: A bearish reversal pattern that forms after an uptrend. Price touches a resistance level twice, creating an 'M' shape.
doubleTop.afterCompletion: After the neckline breaks down, expect a downward move equal to the pattern height. Target = Neckline - (Top - Neckline).
doubleTop.tradingTip: Wait for neckline break with volume confirmation. Place stop above the second top.

headAndShoulders.name: Head & Shoulders
headAndShoulders.description: A bearish reversal pattern with three peaks - the middle peak (head) being the highest.
headAndShoulders.afterCompletion: After neckline break, expect price to fall by the distance from head to neckline.
headAndShoulders.tradingTip: Enter on neckline break. Stop above right shoulder. Target = Neckline - Pattern Height.

inverseHeadAndShoulders.name: Inverse Head & Shoulders
inverseHeadAndShoulders.description: A bullish reversal pattern with three troughs - the middle trough (head) being the lowest.
inverseHeadAndShoulders.afterCompletion: After neckline break, expect price to rise by the distance from head to neckline.
inverseHeadAndShoulders.tradingTip: Enter on neckline break. Stop below right shoulder. Target = Neckline + Pattern Height.

ascendingTriangle.name: Ascending Triangle
ascendingTriangle.description: A bullish continuation pattern with flat resistance and rising support, showing buyers gaining strength.
ascendingTriangle.afterCompletion: Breakout above resistance typically leads to a move equal to the triangle's height.
ascendingTriangle.tradingTip: Enter on breakout above resistance with volume. Stop below the last higher low.

descendingTriangle.name: Descending Triangle
descendingTriangle.description: A bearish continuation pattern with flat support and falling resistance, showing sellers gaining strength.
descendingTriangle.afterCompletion: Breakdown below support typically leads to a move equal to the triangle's height.
descendingTriangle.tradingTip: Enter on breakdown below support with volume. Stop above the last lower high.

symmetricalTriangle.name: Symmetrical Triangle
symmetricalTriangle.description: A neutral pattern that can break either way. Converging trendlines show indecision.
symmetricalTriangle.afterCompletion: Breakout direction determines the move. Target = Breakout point ± Triangle height.
symmetricalTriangle.tradingTip: Wait for clear breakout with volume. Don't anticipate direction.

bullFlag.name: Bull Flag
bullFlag.description: A bullish continuation pattern. After a strong move up (flagpole), price consolidates in a downward channel (flag).
bullFlag.afterCompletion: Expect a continuation move equal to the flagpole length.
bullFlag.tradingTip: Enter on break above flag resistance. Stop below flag low. Target = Breakout + Flagpole.

bearFlag.name: Bear Flag
bearFlag.description: A bearish continuation pattern. After a strong move down (flagpole), price consolidates in an upward channel (flag).
bearFlag.afterCompletion: Expect a continuation move equal to the flagpole length.
bearFlag.tradingTip: Enter on break below flag support. Stop above flag high. Target = Breakdown - Flagpole.

wedge.name: Wedge
wedge.description: Converging trendlines both sloping in the same direction. Rising wedge is bearish, falling wedge is bullish.
wedge.afterCompletion: Breakout opposite to wedge direction. Move typically equals wedge's widest point.
wedge.tradingTip: Trade the breakout in opposite direction of wedge slope.

cupAndHandle.name: Cup and Handle
cupAndHandle.description: A bullish continuation pattern resembling a tea cup. The cup forms a rounded bottom, followed by a small pullback (handle).
cupAndHandle.afterCompletion: Breakout above handle resistance targets cup depth added to breakout level.
cupAndHandle.tradingTip: Enter on handle breakout. Stop below handle low. Long-term bullish signal.

rsiDivergence.name: RSI Divergence
rsiDivergence.description: Price makes new highs/lows but RSI doesn't confirm, signaling potential reversal.
rsiDivergence.afterCompletion: Bullish divergence suggests upward reversal. Bearish divergence suggests downward reversal.
rsiDivergence.tradingTip: Use as confirmation with price action. Don't trade divergence alone.

macdDivergence.name: MACD Divergence
macdDivergence.description: Price makes new highs/lows but MACD histogram doesn't confirm, signaling momentum weakness.
macdDivergence.afterCompletion: Expect trend reversal in direction opposite to the current trend.
macdDivergence.tradingTip: Combine with support/resistance levels for better entries.

breakout.name: Breakout
breakout.description: Price breaks through a significant support or resistance level with increased volume.
breakout.afterCompletion: Expect continuation in breakout direction. Failed breakouts reverse sharply.
breakout.tradingTip: Confirm with volume. Wait for retest of broken level for safer entry.

channelBreak.name: Channel Break
channelBreak.description: Price breaks out of an established trading channel, signaling trend acceleration or reversal.
channelBreak.afterCompletion: Move typically equals channel width in breakout direction.
channelBreak.tradingTip: Trade in breakout direction. Stop inside the channel.

orderBlock.subtitle: Order Blocks & FVG
orderBlock.infoAlgoDesc: Uses Smart Money Concepts (SMC): Detects fractal swing points → measures ATR-normalized displacement → identifies order blocks with CHoCH/BOS structure breaks → scores each zone (0-100) based on displacement strength, structure confirmation, FVG presence, and volume ratio. Only zones scoring 50+ with ≤2 retests are shown.
orderBlock.infoBullishDesc: Zone where institutional buyers entered. Price tends to bounce from these levels. Look for LONG entries when price returns here.
orderBlock.infoBearishDesc: Zone where institutional sellers entered. Price tends to reject from these levels. Look for SHORT entries when price returns here.
orderBlock.infoFvgDesc: Imbalance zones where price moved too fast. Price often returns to fill these gaps before continuing.
orderBlock.infoChochDesc: Change of Character - potential trend reversal detected via ATR displacement
orderBlock.infoBosDesc: Break of Structure - price breaks previous swing high/low, confirming trend continuation
orderBlock.infoScoreDesc: Higher score = stronger zone (look for 70+). Based on displacement, CHoCH, BOS, FVG, and volume.
orderBlock.infoScoring2: Displacement strength: up to +30 points (ATR-normalized move size)
orderBlock.infoScoring5: FVG presence: +5 points | Volume spike: up to +5 points
orderBlock.infoTip: Best entries: Price returns to OB + FVG overlap + CHoCH/BOS confirmation = high probability trade.

clearTrend.title: Cyberpunk Trend Analysis
clearTrend.description: Real-time trend analysis panel combining EMA crossovers, channel positions, and support/resistance levels. Provides a clear directional bias for NASDAQ, XAU/USD and DAX with visual confidence indicators.
clearTrend.dataPoints: EMA 20/50/200 distances, trend channel upper/lower bands, support/resistance proximity, RSI, trend strength percentage, and overall directional signal (BUY/SELL/HOLD).
clearTrend.usage: Check the main signal direction and confidence level before entering a trade. Use the EMA distances to gauge how extended price is from the mean. If price is near channel boundaries, expect reversals.
clearTrend.tips: When all EMAs align (20>50>200 or 20<50<200) with 80%+ confidence, the signal is strongest. Always cross-check with the SMC panel for institutional confirmation.

pulse.title: Pulse 1 - Algorithmic Scalp
pulse.description: 6-component scoring system for fast scalping decisions. Uses SCOUT (initial detection) and CONFIRM (validation) phases to generate short-term trading signals with real-time price updates.
pulse.dataPoints: Price change over 5 minutes, support/resistance levels, momentum score, volume analysis, AI-generated instant comment with target/stop levels, and overall signal strength.
pulse.usage: Watch for SCOUT signals first — they indicate potential setups. When a signal transitions to CONFIRM, it's time to consider entry. The AI comment provides specific target and stop levels.
pulse.tips: Best used during high-volume market hours (US open, London open). Ignore signals during low-volume periods. If momentum and volume disagree, wait for alignment.

pulseV3.title: Pulse 3 - Hybrid Scalp
pulseV3.description: Multi-timeframe hybrid scalping system that combines 3 different timeframes for more reliable signals. Updates every 30 seconds with entry zones, targets, and stop levels.
pulseV3.dataPoints: 3-timeframe analysis, directional signal (BUY/SELL/NEUTRAL), entry zones, target/stop levels, signal validity period, signal strength (STRONG/WATCH/WAIT).
pulseV3.usage: Wait for STRONG SIGNAL status before entering. Check entry zones for optimal positioning. The validity timer shows how long the signal remains actionable — don't enter after it expires.
pulseV3.tips: Pulse V3 works best when its signal aligns with Pulse 1. When both agree on direction with strong confidence, the trade has the highest probability of success.

pulseMl.title: Pulse ML - Machine Learning
pulseMl.description: Machine learning-powered prediction panel that analyzes multiple technical indicators through a trained model. Provides directional predictions with confidence scores and detailed reasoning.
pulseMl.dataPoints: ML prediction direction, confidence percentage, entry/target/stop levels, model scores (technical, momentum, trend), reasoning breakdown (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, volume conditions).
pulseMl.usage: Focus on the confidence percentage — above 75% indicates high-probability setups. Read the reasoning section to understand WHY the model is making its prediction. Use provided entry/target/stop for position management.
pulseMl.tips: ML predictions are most reliable when the model score components (technical, momentum, trend) all agree. If they conflict, the prediction may be less reliable — reduce position size.

emel.title: EMEL Analysis Mode
emel.description: Strategic 9-checkpoint analysis system designed for controlled, methodical trading decisions. Each checkpoint must pass for a valid signal, reducing false entries significantly.
emel.dataPoints: Signal direction, confidence level, price, overall score, 9 individual checkpoint results (each with pass/fail status), decision reasoning, and timing guidance.
emel.usage: Review all 9 checkpoints before considering a trade. The panel tells you WHEN to trade (timing) and WHY (reasoning). If fewer than 7 checkpoints pass, consider waiting or using Pulse mode for faster opportunities.
emel.tips: EMEL is your most conservative signal. When EMEL gives a strong signal with 8-9 checkpoints passing, it's usually a high-quality setup. Use for swing trades and larger positions.

patternEngine.title: Pattern Engine V2
patternEngine.description: Advanced chart pattern detection engine that identifies 15+ classical patterns (double tops, head & shoulders, triangles, flags, etc.) across multiple timeframes with completion tracking.
patternEngine.dataPoints: Pattern name, type (bullish/bearish/neutral), completion percentage, success rate, risk/reward ratio, entry/target/stop zones, detection date, and current stage.
patternEngine.usage: Focus on patterns with 60%+ completion and historical success rates above 65%. The stage indicator shows where the pattern is in its lifecycle. Wait for 'Confirmed' stage before entering.
patternEngine.tips: Combine pattern signals with SMC zones for the best entries. A bullish pattern completing near a bullish order block is a high-conviction trade.

claudePatterns.title: Claude AI Pattern Analysis
claudePatterns.description: AI-powered multi-timeframe pattern analysis using Claude. Provides deeper insight into chart formations with contextual market analysis that goes beyond algorithmic detection.
claudePatterns.dataPoints: AI-identified patterns, multi-timeframe analysis, pattern context, market structure assessment.
claudePatterns.usage: Run analysis when you want a second opinion on current market structure. Claude provides nuanced analysis that considers broader market context beyond just technical patterns.
claudePatterns.tips: Best used after checking Pattern Engine V2 — Claude can validate or challenge the algorithmic findings. If both agree, the pattern is more reliable.

sentiment.title: Market Sentiment
sentiment.description: Real-time market sentiment analysis combining news flow, volatility metrics, and macro indicators. Claude AI interprets the overall market mood to help gauge directional bias.
sentiment.dataPoints: Sentiment direction (bullish/bearish/neutral), news flow summary, volatility assessment, macro economic context.
sentiment.usage: Use as a confirmation tool — don't trade solely on sentiment. When sentiment aligns with your technical analysis, it adds confidence. When it contradicts, be cautious and reduce size.
sentiment.tips: Extreme sentiment readings often precede reversals. When everyone is bullish, look for bearish divergences. When everyone is bearish, look for bullish setups.

news.title: MarketAux Live News
news.description: Live news feed from MarketAux delivering real-time market headlines with sentiment classification. Each headline is tagged as bullish, bearish, or neutral for quick scanning.
news.dataPoints: News headlines, source, publication time, sentiment tag (bullish/bearish/neutral).
news.usage: Scan headlines before and during trading sessions. Focus on news that directly affects your trading instruments (NASDAQ, XAU/USD, DAX). Use sentiment tags for quick assessment.
news.tips: Be cautious of trading immediately after major news — wait for the initial volatility to settle. News creates opportunities but also traps for impulsive traders.

comexNews.title: COMEX & Gold News
comexNews.description: Specialized news panel focusing on COMEX data and gold-specific news. Tracks institutional changes, COT data impacts, and physical gold market developments.
comexNews.dataPoints: COMEX-specific headlines, gold deliveries, institutional positioning changes, COT report impacts.
comexNews.usage: Essential for XAU/USD trading. Check before gold trades for any institutional-level changes. COMEX delivery data can signal potential supply/demand shifts.
comexNews.tips: Large changes in COMEX inventories often precede significant gold price moves. Watch for delivery anomalies and position concentration changes.

whaleTracker.title: Whale Tracker
whaleTracker.description: Tracks large institutional positions and unusual market activity. Identifies potential 'whale' movements that can significantly impact price direction.
whaleTracker.dataPoints: Active whale alerts, institutional position changes, large order flow detection, pressure reading (-1.0 to +1.0 scale).
whaleTracker.usage: Check the pressure reading: positive values indicate buying pressure (bullish), negative values indicate selling pressure (bearish). Active alerts highlight recent institutional activity.
whaleTracker.tips: Updates every Friday with COT data. Whale movements often front-run major price moves by 1-3 days. When whale pressure aligns with technical signals, expect stronger moves.

institutional.title: Institutional Data Panel
institutional.description: Comprehensive institutional positioning data showing how large market participants (hedge funds, banks, commercial traders) are positioned across key markets.
institutional.dataPoints: Net positions by trader type, position changes over time, long/short ratios, historical positioning trends.
institutional.usage: Follow the smart money — when institutional traders increase long positions significantly, it's a bullish signal. Extreme positioning often precedes reversals.
institutional.tips: Don't fight institutional flow. If institutions are net long and adding, the path of least resistance is up. Use extreme readings as contrarian indicators.

candlestick.title: Candlestick Pattern Analysis
candlestick.description: Real-time candlestick pattern detection identifying classical formations (doji, hammer, engulfing, etc.) with ML-adjusted confidence levels and actionable descriptions.
candlestick.dataPoints: Pattern name, direction (bullish/bearish/neutral), signal strength, ML confidence adjustment, pattern description, and recommended action.
candlestick.usage: Filter by direction (bullish/bearish) to focus on relevant patterns. Check ML confidence adjustment — it shows how much the ML model agrees with the traditional interpretation.
candlestick.tips: Single candlestick patterns are less reliable than multi-candle patterns. An engulfing pattern at a key support/resistance level is much more significant than one in the middle of a range.

advancedAnalysis.title: Advanced Detailed Analysis
advancedAnalysis.description: Comprehensive technical analysis panel combining Claude AI and ML predictions with detailed risk management guidance. Provides entry/target/stop levels with thesis reasoning.
advancedAnalysis.dataPoints: Technical indicators, market structure, volume analysis, EMA distances, support/resistance levels, Claude/ML confidence and direction, risk management (position size, R:R), bull/bear thesis.
advancedAnalysis.usage: This is your most detailed panel — review it before taking any significant trade. The thesis summary explains the reasoning. Check volume confirmation to validate price movements.
advancedAnalysis.tips: Pay special attention to the volume warning indicator. Low-volume price moves are often traps. When both Claude and ML agree with strong confidence, it's a high-conviction setup.

strategyPerformance.title: Strategy Performance
strategyPerformance.description: Historical performance tracking for all trading strategies. Monitors accuracy, win rates, and profit/loss across different timeframes and models.
strategyPerformance.dataPoints: Strategy win rate, accuracy percentage, total trades, profit/loss, performance comparison between ML and Claude models.
strategyPerformance.usage: Review weekly to understand which strategies are performing best in current market conditions. Adjust your trading to favor strategies with higher recent accuracy.
strategyPerformance.tips: A strategy that was accurate last month may not be accurate this month. Markets change — regularly review and adapt your approach based on this data.

smc.title: Smart Money Concepts (SMC)
smc.description: Institutional-grade analysis using Smart Money Concepts including order blocks, fair value gaps (FVG), change of character (CHoCH), and break of structure (BOS). Scores each zone 0-100.
smc.dataPoints: Bullish/bearish order blocks with scores, FVG zones, CHoCH/BOS structure signals, combined SMC signal, entry confidence, support/resistance zones.
smc.usage: Look for high-scoring order blocks (70+) near current price. When price returns to an order block with FVG overlap, it's a high-probability entry zone. CHoCH signals indicate potential trend changes.
smc.tips: The best SMC entries combine: price at order block + FVG present + CHoCH/BOS confirmation. Score 80+ zones with all 3 confirmations are institutional-quality setups.

mtfMatrix.title: Multi-Timeframe Matrix
mtfMatrix.description: Visual matrix showing trend alignment across multiple timeframes. When all timeframes agree on direction, the signal strength is maximized for higher-probability trades.
mtfMatrix.dataPoints: Direction per timeframe (5m, 15m, 1H, 4H, Daily), alignment percentage, overall bias, individual timeframe strength.
mtfMatrix.usage: Trade in the direction of the majority alignment. When 4+ timeframes agree, it's a strong signal. When timeframes conflict, it's usually best to wait or reduce position size.
mtfMatrix.tips: The 4H and Daily timeframes carry more weight. If they disagree with lower timeframes, trust the higher timeframes for swing trades. For scalps, focus on 5m and 15m alignment.

riskReward.title: Risk/Reward Calculator
riskReward.description: Dynamic risk/reward analysis panel that calculates optimal position sizing, risk percentage, and expected return based on current technical levels and account parameters.
riskReward.dataPoints: Entry price, target(s), stop loss, risk/reward ratio, position size recommendation, risk percentage of account, expected profit/loss in dollar terms.
riskReward.usage: Never take a trade with R:R below 1.5:1. Use the calculator to size your position according to your risk tolerance. The recommended stop levels are based on current technical analysis.
riskReward.tips: Professional traders risk 1-2% of their account per trade maximum. Even with a 40% win rate, a 3:1 R:R ratio will be profitable long-term.

cotWhale.title: COT Whale Analysis
cotWhale.description: Commitment of Traders (COT) report analysis showing how commercial hedgers, large speculators, and small traders are positioned. Identifies potential positioning extremes.
cotWhale.dataPoints: Net positions by category, weekly changes, historical extremes, positioning percentile, open interest changes.
cotWhale.usage: Commercial traders are typically the 'smart money' — follow their positioning for longer-term trades. Extreme positioning by speculators often signals a potential reversal.
cotWhale.tips: COT data is released every Friday for positions as of Tuesday. There's a 3-day lag — use it for weekly/swing trade planning, not intraday decisions.

seasonality.title: Seasonality Analysis
seasonality.description: Historical seasonal pattern analysis showing how assets typically perform during specific months, weeks, or time periods. Based on multi-year historical data.
seasonality.dataPoints: Monthly/seasonal patterns, historical win rates per period, average returns, seasonal strength indicators.
seasonality.usage: Use as a background filter — trade in the direction of seasonal tendencies when they align with your technical analysis. Don't trade against strong seasonal patterns without good reason.
seasonality.tips: Seasonal patterns work because of institutional flows (quarter-end rebalancing, tax-loss selling, holiday effects). They're most reliable in mature, liquid markets like NASDAQ, Gold, and DAX.

learningDashboard.title: Learning Dashboard
learningDashboard.description: AI learning and self-improvement panel that tracks prediction accuracy over time. Shows how the ML and Claude models are performing, where they agree, and which predictions hit targets.
learningDashboard.dataPoints: Total predictions, accuracy percentages, ML vs Claude comparison, consensus agreement rate, target level hit rates by timeframe, recent prediction results.
learningDashboard.usage: Review regularly to understand model reliability. If a model's accuracy drops below 50%, consider giving more weight to the other model. Track which timeframes produce the best predictions.
learningDashboard.tips: The learning system improves over time as more data accumulates. Models that agree tend to be more accurate. If accuracy for a specific asset consistently drops, the market regime may have changed.

signalCard.title: Live Signal Card
signalCard.description: Real-time signal overview card showing key technical levels and directional bias at a glance. Provides instant access to EMA distances, support/resistance, and channel positions.
signalCard.dataPoints: Current price, trend direction, nearest support/resistance, EMA 20/50/200 distances, channel upper/lower bands, S/R bias.
signalCard.usage: Use as your primary dashboard for quick market assessment. Green metrics indicate bullish conditions, red indicates bearish. The further price is from EMAs, the more extended the move.
signalCard.tips: When support and resistance are very close together (narrow range), expect a breakout soon. The direction will be determined by volume and momentum — watch the Pulse panels for confirmation.
